target_name: Payout mix with neutral non payers
rationale: The COALESCE-to-zero convention is a defensible neutral placement for non-choosers rather than a pure coverage patch, but the claimed coverage gain is contingent on 0/0 (not NaN inputs) driving the missingness — if prstkc/dvt are absent the fallback is equally undefined — and the resulting large tie block at the midpoint makes this only a modest, partly mechanical variation on the already-tested assets-scaled intensity version.

The level-versus-change decomposition of the winning mechanism is a legitimate and informative question, though it closely parallels the archive's "Financing policy reversal at cheap prices" (which already differenced a financing flow and produced only t=1.77) and differencing a ratio defined only for payers will further shrink an already 8% coverage sample.

target_name: Payout mix at a composite discount
rationale: Replacing the single E/P leg with a blended earnings-and-book yield is a coherent measurement-error argument and is internally consistent, but it is an incremental swap of one leg of the winning signal rather than a new mechanism, and the stated link to the "generation 1 negative-alpha lesson" is rhetorical rather than substantive.

target_name: Distribute rather than hoard when cheap
rationale: The expression contradicts its hypothesis: with zero payout and a large cash drawdown the ratio hits its maximum of +1, so firms burning cash to fund losses or capex — precisely the distress case the proposal claims to repair — score in the extreme long leg alongside genuine distributors.

The complementarity test between mix and magnitude is a fair open question, but the added leg is essentially total payout yield — itself a well-known published anomaly and strongly correlated with the E/P leg — so a positive result risks being a repackaged payout-yield/value effect, and multiplying three [0,1] ranks concentrates the long leg in a thin, potentially unstable cell.

target_name: Payout mix against own price history
rationale: Swapping the cross-sectional price benchmark for a within-firm one is the sharpest available test of whether the winning result is managerial timing or amplified HML exposure, and it differs meaningfully from the earlier own-trough signal that paired timing with repurchase intensity rather than instrument choice, though the coarse five-point TS_RANK and the weak alpha of that earlier attempt temper expectations.
